correctness.rationale: In the monomial basis the residue chains reduce both the operator and its adjoint. Phase removal gives one positive Gram chain B=D_q T D_q with tridiagonal Toeplitz T. Its one-coordinate tail is q²B, giving normalized squared eigenvalues x_j that decrease, by min–max interlacing. Principal minors split into consecutive runs; each length-l determinant satisfies the stated two-term continuant recurrence and is sum_{h=0}^l a^(2h). In trace class the order-n principal minors sum to the trace of the nth exterior power. Its norm is the product of the n largest eigenvalues and bounds below that trace; the leading coordinate wedge supplies the lower bound on the norm. The normalized leading products lie between 1 and a q,a-dependent constant for 0<a<1: each run contributes at most (1-a²)^(-1), v runs require displacement at least v(v-1)/2, and the weighted partition sum is finite since q²<1. At a=1 the product is at least n+1; the same run bound gives a subexponential upper bound, by absorbing exp(sqrt(2L) log(n+1)) into q^(2L) with the stated completing-the-square estimate. Thus the monotone x_j have limit 1 and are at least 1. Bounded log products are equivalent to summability of sqrt(x_j)-1 on their bounded range; divergence at a=1 follows from the leading product, and monotonicity of summable excess gives o(1/j). There is also entrywise Gram duality B(a)=a² B(1/a), confirming the paper's isometry argument. For finite m the lists r^{mk+b} h_k have a strictly geometric separation eventually because M≤h_k<M/r. Once the finite head is passed, all earlier terms outnumber the tail by exactly the corresponding index offset, so the natural ranks are correct. Coordinatewise comparison with the geometric baseline also survives rearrangement for the whole sequence. Jensen's formula, or integrating the unit-circle logarithm at the boundary zero, gives M. Finite reproduction gave 924 exact rational determinant/composition checks; a separate analytic check bounds the critical normalized squared product above by C_q(n+1), sharpening but not needed for the frozen proof. The 'one-tap' label denotes one residue chain (m=1); the weight still has two monomials.
residual_risks: The finite checks do not verify the spectrum at all indices or the infinite limit. Results are at fixed parameters and neither a critical individual coefficient nor uniformity near q=1 is claimed. An in-script comment denying literal entrywise duality is inaccurate for the real positive Gram parameter (both diagonal and off-diagonal scale exactly); this does not affect script assertions or the proof.

evidence: The chain's singular values are the positive eigenvalues of the selfadjoint block operator with off-diagonal blocks A and A*. Interlacing the output and input bases gives a zero-diagonal Jacobi matrix with successive couplings q^j, a q^j, q^{j+1}, a q^{j+1}, … . Kozhan's theorem uses successive ratios tending to zero; here they alternate between a and q/a. The Hahn–Exton paper's displayed Jacobi family has coefficients growing as q^{-n}, not the decaying compact Gram coefficients.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Kozhan's asymptotic theorem is genuinely related after a change of representation, but its hypothesis fails for every fixed q,a here. value.rationale: For a canonical compact weighted composition model, eigenvalue or Schatten estimates do not give this high-rank singular-value scale. The coefficient captures the interior versus exterior factorization of the Hardy weight, while the total excess sharply detects a boundary zero even when the same first-order coefficient holds. The block interlacing and determinant-growth explanation are useful quantitative spectral information distinct from a routine compactness or Schatten check.
residual_risks: Only two monomials and fixed spacing and radius are assessed; no general polynomial-weight or per-eigenvalue critical error law is inferred.
